record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a truncated file listing only; code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes after weight edits, bearing on the practical weight-edit version, but does not report the original activation ablation or addition procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports three weight-edit conditions with refusal outcomes. Other reported quantities, including W05 spectral scores, direction cosines, and edit-detection rates, are not rows because they do not measure the refusal behavior named by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly a weight-spectrum detector for edited checkpoints, so most of its results are detector statistics. It does report refusal rates after refusal-direction weight edits (Root B, Householder) and a behavioural check on declared-uncensored Hub checkpoints. These bear weakly on V2 in a new setting: depth-weighted and isometric kernels plus released Hub edits.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a parent-free spectral certificate is a precision instrument, not a safety score: it dissociates from refusal in both directions, and isometric edits are provably invisible to it. They retract the windowed recall headline (0.700 vs 0.300) as a depth/architecture confound; depth-matched figures are 0.387 vs 0.290.
record.recipe_differences: This is a repository about detecting edited safety models using weight-space spectral statistics. The reported refusal outcomes follow weight edits; the README does not report the original activation-direction projection or addition recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports differing refusal outcomes across edit conditions: Root B, Householder, and Root C.

fits_no_version.finding: 200 benign LoRA steps on an abliterated checkpoint restore refusal, while the spectral scar barely moves (-4.592→-4.381).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration-removed refusal can be restored by small benign fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: A 5-bit quantization of an abliterated model gives refusal 0.237 (ppl 26.25→28.77), with cos(v1,r)>0.9994.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal removal by abliteration survives quantization.

record.problems: The repository code was not read or run. The README does not supply model-level details for some reported aggregate/edit conditions, a refusal baseline for the Householder result, or a general-capability assessment for these edits.
record.rows_left_out: No additional refusal outcomes from the README were omitted. Statistics about detector performance, spectral scores, and direction alignment were excluded because they do not measure a claim-version refusal outcome.

untested.parts: Capability preservation after the edits (only one perplexity figure, for the 5-bit quantized case). Per-model refusal for released Hub abliterations beyond the 14-checkpoint behavioural check.
Activation-level ablation or addition of the diff-in-means direction; general capability.

missing.what: Behavioural check of 14 stratified declared-uncensored Hub checkpoints: 4 verified uncensored, 3 not uncensored, 5 ambiguous, 1 incoherent, 1 failure.
Root B refusal under alternative judges: 0.278 archived, 0.772 cross-family, 0.195 re-worded.
Refusal 0.237 after 5-bit quantization of an abliterated model; benign LoRA restoring refusal.

record.verdict_notes: Mostly a detector study; refusal numbers serve as manipulation checks on in-house edits. The code and result files were not read, so the README text is the only evidence. Detector statistics (W05, recall, AUROC) are correctly excluded from rows.

versions.untested_parts: No all-layer, all-position activation projection of the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction, and no addition of that direction or general-capability assessment.
The README does not establish that the reported edits are the specified conversion of the original ablation into a weight edit or that the results generalize to released models.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is carried by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test of the refusal direction.
No test of how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.

rows.subject: Root B (n=111 declared Hub edits)
rows.operation_detail: Depth-weighted Gaussian edit with direction held fixed
rows.note: The README describes this as uncensoring, with the direction held fixed; it does not identify the exact checkpoint names in the aggregate.
rows.check: Refusal 0.950→0.270 depends on the scorer: 0.278 archived judge, 0.772 cross-family judge, 0.195 re-worded rubric. The cross-family value shows a much weaker removal. The subject is in-house kernels on a host model; per S4, n=111 is the prompt count, not 111 Hub edits. The 45.8% prevalence refers to the class's share of declared Hub edits.

source_check.correct: Root B is one checkpoint the authors built (depth-weighted Gaussian edit, direction held fixed) on an unnamed parent. n=111 is the sample behind the refusal rate 0.270 [0.196,0.360]; the interval matches 30/111. 45.8% is how common this recipe class is among declared Hub edits, not the scored population. The 0.270 is under the archived judge: re-scored 0.278 archived, 0.772 cross-family judge, 0.195 re-worded rubric, all below the parent.
source_check.problem: The record treats Root B as 111 declared Hub edits, but it is one in-house checkpoint scored on n=111, under the archived judge.
